podcast.body: This was Elvis Presley's final hit single released during his lifetime, recorded during a notorious session in October 1976 in the "Jungle Room" at Graceland. Despite the session being described as a "disaster" due to Elvis's lack of focus, his struggles with weight, anxiety, and prescription drugs, and eccentric behavior (like testing motorcycles and playfully threatening speakers with a machine gun), the song achieved significant success. It became a number one country hit and reached number 31 on the Billboard Top 40 for the week ending August 6, 1977. After his death on August 16, 1977, the song re-entered the charts and climbed to number 18 on the Hot 100. Gospel legend J.D. Sumner provided a deep bass vocal on the track, which critics describe as a "more mature Elvis" with a country-pop mix. "It was a number one country hit. It made it to number 31 on the Billboard Top 40 for the week ending August 6, 1977."
